title: Supersedure and restart semantics
preamble:
# Supersedure and restart semantics

The `as <expr>` clause on `call` and
`after`, and the per-fact supersedure semantics it produces.

`as` is the DS correlation/identity-key keyword. One concept,
two surfaces:

- `call ... as <expr>` — call correlation, drives response-fact
  supersedure per [LCRS.6.2] and capture-fact supersedure per
  [LCCO.5].
- `after <dur> as <expr>:` — synthetic timer correlation,
  drives timer supersedure on re-fire.

Mental model: **correlation identity drives supersedure.** A
new assertion of a fact with the same correlation as an
existing fact retracts the prior fact. The mechanism is
per-fact.

Paired with:
- [LTAC] — `after`-clause grammar.
- [LCRS] — `call as` correlation
  semantics and response-fact supersedure at [LCRS.6.2].
- [LCCO.5] —
  capture-fact lifecycle.
- [LSCP] — `scope activation`, the
  lifetime of the facts an activation asserts.
- [LEXP] — the `as <expr>` evaluation
  context (snapshot at activation start).

## What this is not

- Not a cascade-cancellation primitive. The activation has no
  lifetime as a unit beyond its scope-activation facts'
  individual lifetimes.
- Not a queueing surface. `as`-supersedure replaces the prior
  artefact; it does not buffer.
